paragraphs.text: After he had ended all his sayings in the ears of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
paragraphs.original: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
paragraphs.translit: Epeidē eplērōsen panta ta rhēmata autou eis tas akoas tou laou, eisēlthen eis Kapharnaoum.

paragraphs.text: And a certain centurion`s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick and at the point of death.
paragraphs.original: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.
paragraphs.translit: Hekatontarchou de tinos doulos kakōs echōn ēmellen teleutan, hos ēn autō entimos.

paragraphs.text: And when he heard concerning Jesus, he sent unto him elders of the Jews, asking him that he would come and save his servant.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de peri tou Iēsou apesteilen pros auton presbyterous tōn Ioudaiōn, erōtōn auton hopōs elthōn diasōsē ton doulon autou.

paragraphs.text: And they, when they came to Jesus, besought him earnestly, saying, He is worthy that thou shouldest do this for him;
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο,
paragraphs.translit: hoi de paragenomenoi pros ton Iēsoun parekaloun auton spoudaiōs legontes hoti Axios estin hō parexē touto,

paragraphs.text: for he loveth our nation, and himself built us our synagogue.
paragraphs.original: ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: agapa gar to ethnos hēmōn kai tēn synagōgēn autos ōkodomēsen hēmin.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself; for I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof:
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς. ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου, οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eporeueto syn autois. ēdē de autou ou makran apechontos apo tēs oikias epempsen philous ho hekatontarchēs legōn autō· Kyrie, mē skyllou, ou gar hikanos eimi hina hypo tēn stegēn mou eiselthēs·

paragraphs.text: wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say the word, and my servant shall be healed.
paragraphs.original: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν· ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου·
paragraphs.translit: dio oude emauton ēxiōsa pros se elthein· alla eipe logō, kai iathētō ho pais mou·

paragraphs.text: For I also am a man set under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπʼ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar egō anthrōpos eimi hypo exousian tassomenos, echōn hypʼ emauton stratiōtas, kai legō toutō· Poreuthēti, kai poreuetai, kai allō· Erchou, kai erchetai, kai tō doulō mou· Poiēson touto, kai poiei.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned and said unto the multitude that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de tauta ho Iēsous ethaumasen auton, kai strapheis tō akolouthounti autō ochlō eipen· Legō hymin, oude en tō Israēl tosautēn pistin heuron.

paragraphs.text: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες εὗρον τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα.
paragraphs.translit: kai hypostrepsantes eis ton oikon hoi pemphthentes heuron ton doulon hygiainonta.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass soon afterwards, that he went to a city called Nain; and his disciples went with him, and a great multitude.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en tō hexēs eporeuthē eis polin kaloumenēn Nain, kai syneporeuonto autō hoi mathētai autou kai ochlos polys.

paragraphs.text: Now when he drew near to the gate of the city, behold, there was carried out one that was dead, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς μονογενὴς υἱὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὴ ἦν χήρα, καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de ēngisen tē pylē tēs poleōs, kai idou exekomizeto tethnēkōs monogenēs hyios tē mētri autou, kai autē ēn chēra, kai ochlos tēs poleōs hikanos ēn syn autē.

paragraphs.text: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μὴ κλαῖε.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn autēn ho kyrios esplanchnisthē epʼ autē kai eipen autē· Mē klaie.

paragraphs.text: And he came nigh and touched the bier: and the bearers stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ, οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν, καὶ εἶπεν· Νεανίσκε, σοὶ λέγω, ἐγέρθητι.
paragraphs.translit: kai proselthōn hēpsato tēs sorou, hoi de bastazontes estēsan, kai eipen· Neaniske, soi legō, egerthēti.

paragraphs.text: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai anekathisen ho nekros kai ērxato lalein, kai edōken auton tē mētri autou.

paragraphs.text: And fear took hold on all: and they glorified God, saying, A great prophet is arisen among us: and, God hath visited his people.
paragraphs.original: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: elaben de phobos pantas, kai edoxazon ton theon legontes hoti Prophētēs megas ēgerthē en hēmin, kai hoti Epeskepsato ho theos ton laon autou.

paragraphs.text: And this report went forth concerning him in the whole of Judaea, and all the region round about.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai exēlthen ho logos houtos en holē tē Ioudaia peri autou kai pasē tē perichōrō.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples of John told him of all these things.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων. καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης
paragraphs.translit: Kai apēngeilan Iōannē hoi mathētai autou peri pantōn toutōn. kai proskalesamenos dyo tinas tōn mathētōn autou ho Iōannēs

paragraphs.text: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to the Lord, saying, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?
paragraphs.original: ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;
paragraphs.translit: epempsen pros ton kyrion legōn· Sy ei ho erchomenos ē allon prosdokōmen;

paragraphs.text: And when the men were come unto him, they said, John the Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?
paragraphs.original: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;
paragraphs.translit: paragenomenoi de pros auton hoi andres eipan· Iōannēs ho baptistēs apesteilen hēmas pros se legōn· Sy ei ho erchomenos ē allon prosdokōmen;

paragraphs.text: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and on many that were blind he bestowed sight.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.
paragraphs.translit: en ekeinē tē hōra etherapeusen pollous apo nosōn kai mastigōn kai pneumatōn ponērōn, kai typhlois pollois echarisato blepein.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto them, Go and tell John the things which ye have seen and heard; the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, the poor have good tidings preached to them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε· τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται, κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis eipen autois· Poreuthentes apangeilate Iōannē ha eidete kai ēkousate· typhloi anablepousin, chōloi peripatousin, leproi katharizontai, kōphoi akouousin, nekroi egeirontai, ptōchoi euangelizontai·

paragraphs.text: And blessed is he, whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling in me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.
paragraphs.translit: kai makarios estin hos ean mē skandalisthē en emoi.

paragraphs.text: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to behold? a reed shaken with the wind?
paragraphs.original: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;
paragraphs.translit: Apelthontōn de tōn angelōn Iōannou ērxato legein pros tous ochlous peri Iōannou· Ti exēlthate eis tēn erēmon theasasthai; kalamon hypo anemou saleuomenon;

paragraphs.text: But what went ye out to see? a man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they that are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings` courts.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.
paragraphs.translit: alla ti exēlthate idein; anthrōpon en malakois himatiois ēmphiesmenon; idou hoi en himatismō endoxō kai tryphē hyparchontes en tois basileiois eisin.

paragraphs.text: But what went ye out to see? a prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; προφήτην; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.
paragraphs.translit: alla ti exēlthate idein; prophētēn; nai, legō hymin, kai perissoteron prophētou.

paragraphs.text: This is he of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, Who shall prepare thy way before thee.
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin peri hou gegraptai· Idou apostellō ton angelon mou pro prosōpou sou, hos kataskeuasei tēn hodon sou emprosthen sou.

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there is none greater than John: yet he that is but little in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin, meizōn en gennētois gynaikōn Iōannou oudeis estin· ho de mikroteros en tē basileia tou theou meizōn autou estin.

paragraphs.text: And all the people when they heard, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
paragraphs.original: (καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου·
paragraphs.translit: (kai pas ho laos akousas kai hoi telōnai edikaiōsan ton theon, baptisthentes to baptisma Iōannou·

paragraphs.text: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected for themselves the counsel of God, being not baptized of him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.)
paragraphs.translit: hoi de Pharisaioi kai hoi nomikoi tēn boulēn tou theou ēthetēsan eis heautous, mē baptisthentes hypʼ autou.)

paragraphs.text: Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation, and to what are they like?
paragraphs.original: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;
paragraphs.translit: Tini oun homoiōsō tous anthrōpous tēs geneas tautēs, kai tini eisin homoioi;

paragraphs.text: They are like unto children that sit in the marketplace, and call one to another; who say, We piped unto you, and ye did not dance; we wailed, and ye did not weep.
paragraphs.original: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ἃ λέγει· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·
paragraphs.translit: homoioi eisin paidiois tois en agora kathēmenois kai prosphōnousin allēlois, ha legei· Ēulēsamen hymin kai ouk ōrchēsasthe· ethrēnēsamen kai ouk eklausate·

paragraphs.text: For John the Baptist is come eating no bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a demon.
paragraphs.original: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·
paragraphs.translit: elēlythen gar Iōannēs ho baptistēs mē esthiōn arton mēte pinōn oinon, kai legete· Daimonion echei·

paragraphs.text: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold, a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!
paragraphs.original: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: elēlythen ho hyios tou anthrōpou esthiōn kai pinōn, kai legete· Idou anthrōpos phagos kai oinopotēs, philos telōnōn kai hamartōlōn.

paragraphs.text: And wisdom is justified of all her children.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai edikaiōthē hē sophia apo pantōn tōn teknōn autēs.

paragraphs.text: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he entered into the Pharisee`s house, and sat down to meat.
paragraphs.original: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετʼ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη.
paragraphs.translit: Ērōta de tis auton tōn Pharisaiōn hina phagē metʼ autou· kai eiselthōn eis ton oikon tou Pharisaiou kateklithē.

paragraphs.text: And behold, a woman who was in the city, a sinner; and when she knew that he was sitting at meat in the Pharisee`s house, she brought an alabaster cruse of ointment,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός, καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου
paragraphs.translit: kai idou gynē hētis ēn en tē polei hamartōlos, kai epignousa hoti katakeitai en tē oikia tou Pharisaiou, komisasa alabastron myrou

paragraphs.text: and standing behind at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
paragraphs.original: καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα, τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai stasa opisō para tous podas autou klaiousa, tois dakrysin ērxato brechein tous podas autou kai tais thrixin tēs kephalēs autēs exemassen, kai katephilei tous podas autou kai ēleiphen tō myrō.

paragraphs.text: Now when the Pharisee that had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him, that she is a sinner.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: idōn de ho Pharisaios ho kalesas auton eipen en heautō legōn· Houtos ei ēn prophētēs, eginōsken an tis kai potapē hē gynē hētis haptetai autou, hoti hamartōlos estin.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Teacher, say on.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν. ὁ δέ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen pros auton· Simōn, echō soi ti eipein. ho de· Didaskale, eipe, phēsin.

paragraphs.text: A certain lender had two debtors: the one owed five hundred shillings, and the other fifty.
paragraphs.original: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: dyo chreopheiletai ēsan danistē tini· ho heis ōpheilen dēnaria pentakosia, ho de heteros pentēkonta.

paragraphs.text: When they had not [wherewith] to pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο. τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν;
paragraphs.translit: mē echontōn autōn apodounai amphoterois echarisato. tis oun autōn pleion agapēsei auton;

paragraphs.text: Simon answered and said, He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis Simōn eipen· Hypolambanō hoti hō to pleion echarisato. ho de eipen autō· Orthōs ekrinas.

paragraphs.text: And turning to the woman, he said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thy house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath wetted my feet with her tears, and wiped them with her hair.
paragraphs.original: καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη· Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα; εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, ὕδωρ μοι ἐπὶ πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai strapheis pros tēn gynaika tō Simōni ephē· Blepeis tautēn tēn gynaika; eisēlthon sou eis tēn oikian, hydōr moi epi podas ouk edōkas· hautē de tois dakrysin ebrexen mou tous podas kai tais thrixin autēs exemaxen.

paragraphs.text: Thou gavest me no kiss: but she, since the time I came in, hath not ceased to kiss my feet.
paragraphs.original: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ ἀφʼ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας.
paragraphs.translit: philēma moi ouk edōkas· hautē de aphʼ hēs eisēlthon ou dielipen kataphilousa mou tous podas.

paragraphs.text: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but she hath anointed my feet with ointment.
paragraphs.original: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας· αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας μου.
paragraphs.translit: elaiō tēn kephalēn mou ouk ēleipsas· hautē de myrō ēleipsen tous podas mou.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, [the same] loveth little.
paragraphs.original: οὗ χάριν, λέγω σοι, ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ· ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται, ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ.
paragraphs.translit: hou charin, legō soi, apheōntai hai hamartiai autēs hai pollai, hoti ēgapēsen poly· hō de oligon aphietai, oligon agapa.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autē· Apheōntai sou hai hamartiai.

paragraphs.text: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that even forgiveth sins?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai ērxanto hoi synanakeimenoi legein en heautois· Tis houtos estin hos kai hamartias aphiēsin;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα· Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros tēn gynaika· Hē pistis sou sesōken se· poreuou eis eirēnēn.
